unsupported.what: Table 1 Models 2-3 and Table 2 Model 2: OLS of spending views on the wording dummy with the continuous racial resentment scale and its interactions (e.g. RR 1.46, welfare x RR .37, the triple interaction .10)
unsupported.why: a regression slope on a continuous predictor is not an engine op (meta.engine_requests 'ols_coefficients')

unsupported.what: Table A2 Models 2-3 (split-sample slopes) and the pre-vs-post F tests (F .9, 1.7, 1.2) and coefficient-equality p-values
unsupported.why: continuous-predictor regressions and nested-model F tests are not engine ops

unsupported.what: model-level statistics: omnibus F of Table 2 Model 1 (15.81, p < .001; 3 df) and SI Table A2 Model 1 (61.38, p < .001), the other omnibus F of Tables 1-2 / A2 (464.96, 317.24, 136.75, 207.0, 158.2), and the residual standard errors .79 / .63 (Tables 1-2, A2) and .32 (Table 3)
unsupported.why: a multi-df omnibus F is not an engine op (the 1-df terms are effects); a residual SE is not a target stat (the engine has mean / median / share). Model 1's .79 equals the pooled within-cell SD of spend; not added as a target, because no sd stat exists and a derived equivalence would not be the printed quantity

unsupported.what: Table 3 omnibus F 1.20 (p = .30) for both slopes = 0
unsupported.why: a 2-df F test is not an engine op; its two 1-df contrasts are effects rr_post_assist_t3 and rr_welfare_vs_assist_post_t3
